@maintainers Would it be possible to create a public channel called formalizing Jewish texts?

I have completed a Lean 4 formalization of all sixteen units of Mishnah Kinnim, including the Koppel–Reiss optimization result for Kinnim 3:2:

https://github.com/ashebson/kinin-lean

I would like to see whether a small community can form around formalizing mathematical and logical reasoning found in Jewish texts. The proposed channel would provide a place to discuss Lean development, source interpretation, model fidelity, scholarly review, and possible future texts.

The aim is not to claim that Lean verifies a particular interpretation of a text, but to distinguish clearly between interpretive choices and the deductions that Lean can verify once those choices have been formalized.

Would a dedicated channel be appropriate, or would you prefer that we begin as a topic in an existing channel?
@Patrick Massot would love to get your input

I don’t know why you specifically want my input, but I can tell you our usual rules. When a new project asks for a dedicated channel, we wait until there is evidence that enough people are interested and have enough things to write. So you should start with a thread in the general channel, and ask again if it turns out many people contribute and that thread becomes difficult to follow.
